    94	
    95	/-! ## The sampled triple -/
    96	
    97	/-- The extended line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line of an
    98	extended sample.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

   104	  | .axis => directALineDescOf P.extendedDirectLd s
   105	  | .diagonal => directDLineDescOf P.extendedDirectLd s
   106	
   107	/-- The extended line of a branch, read off the auxiliary randomness.
   108	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   109	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   110	noncomputable def subLineExtLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   111	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) :
   112	    DirectLineDesc P.extendedDirectLd :=
   113	  subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.1.1, k, w.1.2⟩
   114	
   115	/-- A source line of a branch: the canonical axis or diagonal line decoded
   116	from a point block, a scalar seed and a direction block.  Blueprint
   117	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   118	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   119	noncomputable def subLineSourceLine (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   120	    (b : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (s : ScalarQ P.toLdParams)
   121	    (d : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) : LineDesc P.toLdParams :=
   122	  match kind with
   123	  | .axis => aLineDescOfBlock P.toLdParams (b, (s, d))
   124	  | .diagonal => dLineDescOfBlock P.toLdParams (b, (s, d))
   125	
   126	/-- The triple sampled by one branch of the procedure: the extended line
   127	together with the two source lines decoded from its two coordinate blocks and
   128	from the two scalar seeds.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`,
   129	paper `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
   130	-/
   131	noncomputable def subLineTripleOf (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind)
   132	    (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (w : SubLineRaw P) : SubLineTriple P :=
   133	  (subLineExtLine P kind k w,
   134	    (subLineSourceLine P kind (projX (directPointToPauli P w.1.1)) w.2.1
   135	        (projX (directPointToPauli P w.1.2)),
   136	      subLineSourceLine P kind (projZ (directPointToPauli P w.1.1)) w.2.2
   137	        (projZ (directPointToPauli P w.1.2))))
   138	
   139	/-- The law of the triples sampled by one branch.  Blueprint

   223	      sample ∈ (subLineBranchDist P kind).support := by

   233	        (fun w => (k, w))).support) from hkw)

   240	    (Finset.mem_filter.mp hsz).2
   241	  refine ⟨kind, k, w, hx, hz, ?_⟩

     3	/-!
     4	# The projected mixtures of the sub-line law
     5	
     6	This module assembles the two projected point marginals of the sub-line law of
     7	`lem:qld-sublines` into mixtures of the restricted product laws.  Drawing a
     8	uniform point of the extended line of a mixture of line laws is the same
     9	mixture of the corresponding uniform-point laws, so the two projected
    10	marginals of the sub-line law are the mixtures, over the drawn kind and the
    11	drawn extended coordinate, of the projected marginals of one branch at one
    12	extended coordinate.  Each of those is the component law of the pair of
    13	indices carried by that branch, so the mixing law is the law of the kind
    14	together with the pair of indices assigned to a uniform extended coordinate.

    17

    19	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    21	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    22	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.

     7	This module identifies the two projected point marginals of the sub-line law

     9	source lines of a sampled triple depend on the drawn extended point only
    10	through the canonical representatives of its two source blocks, and those
    11	representatives are unchanged when the drawn point is replaced by any point of
    12	the extended line; a uniform point of the extended line through a uniform
    13	point is a uniform point, so the drawn point may be replaced throughout by the
    14	point that is finally retained.  The six generating blocks of the resulting
    15	law -- the two source point blocks, the two scalar seeds and the two source
    16	direction blocks -- are then regrouped into the two restricted product laws
    17	carried by the two indices of the branch.
    18	
    19	## References
    20	
    21	The identification is the last step of the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
    22	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    23	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    24	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    25	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.

    34	noncomputable section
    35	
    36	/-! ## Source lines depend on the point block only through its representative -/

    38	/-- Two source lines of the same branch with the same seed and the same source

    41	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    42	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

    49	        (subLineSourceDirection P kind (chiIndex P.toLdParams s) d) b') :

    53	  · exact lineDesc_diagonal_congr h rfl _ _ _ _

    55	/-- Replacing the drawn extended point by a point of the extended line does

    58	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    59	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

     4	/-!
     5	# Coordinate blocks of an extended point and of an extended direct sample
     6	
     7	This module records the block decomposition used by the sampling procedure of
     8	the sub-line lemma on the extended dimension.  A point of the extended space
     9	is the tuple consisting of its two source point blocks and its two scalar
    10	coordinates, and this decomposition is a bijection carrying the uniform law to
    11	the uniform law; in particular the two source blocks of a uniform extended
    12	point are independent and uniform.  The decomposition is linear, so it
    13	commutes with the affine parameterization of a line, and it commutes with the
    14	canonical identification of the extended scalar field with the source scalar
    15	field.  The stored coordinate index of an extended direct sample splits along
    16	the same three coordinate ranges.
    17	
    18	## References
    19	
    20	The decompositions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    21	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    22	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    23	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    24	445--480, paper lines 970--989.
    25	-/
    26	
    27	open scoped BigOperators
    28	
    29	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    30	
    31	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    32	
    33	noncomputable section
    34	
    35	/-! ## Linearity of the coordinate blocks -/
    36

    38	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/

    41	    (u v : Fin (2 * m + 2) → K) :
    42	    projX (u + v) = projX u + projX v := rfl
    43	
    44	/-- The `Z` block of a sum of extended points is the sum of the blocks.
    45	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    46	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/

    65	/-! ## The coordinate blocks of an extended point -/
    66	
    67	/-- Split an extended point into its two source point blocks and its two
    68	scalar coordinates.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    69	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/

    73	          (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) ×
    74	        (Fin 2 → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :=
    75	  (Equiv.arrowCongr (finCombineEquiv P.m)
    76	      (Equiv.refl (DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))).trans
    77	    ((Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _).trans
    78	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.sumArrowEquivProdArrow _ _ _) (Equiv.refl _)))

   102	    (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).2 1 = u (betaVar P.m) := rfl

   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   107	theorem uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   108	    (uniformDistribution
   109	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   110	        (extendedPointBlockEquiv P) =
   111	      uniformDistribution
   112	        (((Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ×
   113	            (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) ×
   114	          (Fin 2 → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) :=
   115	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv _
   116	
   117	/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly sampled extended point are
   118	independent and uniform.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   119	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   120	theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   121	    (uniformDistribution
   122	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   123	        (fun u => (projX u, projZ u)) =
   124	      Distribution.prod
   125	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd))
   126	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)) := by
   127	  have hfun :

   129	          (projX u, projZ u)) =
   130	        fun u => (extendedPointBlockEquiv P u).1 := by

   133	    exact ⟨(extendedPointBlockEquiv_projX P u).symm,

   135	  rw [hfun, ← Distribution.map_map _ (extendedPointBlockEquiv P) Prod.fst,
   136	    uniformDistribution_map_extendedPointBlockEquiv,

   145	theorem projX_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams)

   163	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   164	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   165	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directLdSpaceIndexEquiv (D : DirectLdParams) :
   166	    (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace D)).map (directLdSpaceIndexEquiv D) =

   169	          ((Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D) × (Fin D.m → DirectScalarQ D))) :=

   173	
   174	/-- An extended line is compatible with two source lines as soon as each of
   175	its two point blocks is an affine reparameterization of the corresponding
   176	source line: the base block is a point of the source line and the direction
   177	block is a multiple of the source direction.  The two scalar coordinates of

   181	`def:combine-map`, paper
   182	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
   183	theorem isCombineLineCompatible_of_blocks {K : Type*} [Field K] {m : ℕ}

   188	      (u (alphaVar m)) (v (alphaVar m)) (u (betaVar m)) (v (betaVar m)) := by
   189	  refine ⟨rfl, rfl, rfl, rfl, fun t => ⟨?_, ?_⟩⟩
   190	  · rw [projX_add, projX_smul, hX, hXv]
   191	    module
   192	  · rw [projZ_add, projZ_smul, hZ, hZv]
   193	    module

   198	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/

     3	/-!
     4	# Uniformity under the identification of the two scalar fields
     5	
     6	The extended line of the sub-line construction lives over the scalar field of
     7	the directly indexed extended game, while the two source lines live over the
     8	scalar field of the Pauli basis test.  The two fields are identified
     9	coordinatewise by a field isomorphism, so that identification is a bijection
    10	of the coordinate spaces and therefore carries uniform laws to uniform laws.
    11	This module records that transport for a whole extended point and for the two
    12	source blocks of an extended point, and it records the resampling rule that
    13	reading a function at the point of a uniformly random affine parameter on the
    14	line through the canonical representative of a uniformly random point is the
    15	same as reading that function at a uniformly random point.
    16	
    17	## References
    18	
    19	The statements support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    20	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    21	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    22	The coordinate blocks are those of `def:combine-map`, blueprint lines
    23	445--480, paper lines 970--989.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	open scoped BigOperators
    27	
    28	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    29	
    30	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    31	
    32	noncomputable section
    33	
    34	/-! ## The identification of the two scalar fields as a bijection -/
    35	
    36	/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
    37	source scalar field on one source block, presented as a bijection.  Blueprint
    38	`def:combine-map`, paper
    39	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    40	noncomputable def directBlockToPauliEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    41	    (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃ (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) where
    42	  toFun v := fun i => extendedDirectScalarEquiv P (v i)
    43	  invFun v := fun i => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).symm (v i)
    44	  left_inv v := by
    45	    funext i
    46	    simp
    47	  right_inv v := by
    48	    funext i
    49	    simp
    50	
    51	/-- The coordinatewise identification of the extended scalar field with the
    52	source scalar field on a whole extended point, presented as a bijection.
    53	Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    54	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    55	noncomputable def directPointToPauliEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    56	    (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) ≃
    57	      (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → PauliScalar P) where
    58	  toFun := directPointToPauli P
    59	  invFun v := fun i => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv P).symm (v i)
    60	  left_inv v := by
    61	    funext i
    62	    simp [directPointToPauli]
    63	  right_inv v := by
    64	    funext i
    65	    simp [directPointToPauli]
    66	
    67	/-- The `X` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `X`
    68	block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    69	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    70	theorem projX_directPointToPauli_eq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    71	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    72	    projX (directPointToPauli P u) = directBlockToPauliEquiv P (projX u) := rfl
    73	
    74	/-- The `Z` block of a transported extended point is the transport of its `Z`
    75	block.  Blueprint `def:combine-map`, paper
    76	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:970-989`. -/
    77	theorem projZ_directPointToPauli_eq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    78	    (u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd) :
    79	    projZ (directPointToPauli P u) = directBlockToPauliEquiv P (projZ u) := rfl
    80	
    81	/-! ## Transport of the uniform laws -/
    82	
    83	/-- A uniformly random extended point transported to the source scalar field
    84	is uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    85	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    86	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directPointToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    87	    (uniformDistribution
    88	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
    89	        (directPointToPauli P) =
    90	      uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → PauliScalar P) :=
    91	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv (directPointToPauliEquiv P)
    92	
    93	/-- A uniformly random source block transported to the source scalar field is
    94	uniformly random.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    95	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    96	theorem uniformDistribution_map_directBlockToPauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
    97	    (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
    98	        (fun v => directBlockToPauliEquiv P v) =
    99	      uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :=
   100	  uniformDistribution_map_equiv (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)
   101	
   102	/-- The two source blocks of a uniformly random extended point, read in the
   103	source scalar field, are independent and uniformly random.  Blueprint
   104	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   105	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   106	theorem uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ_pauli (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   107	    (uniformDistribution
   108	          (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   109	        (fun u => (projX (directPointToPauli P u),
   110	          projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =
   111	      Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P))
   112	        (uniformDistribution (Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)) := by
   113	  classical
   114	  have hfun :
   115	      (fun u : Fin (2 * P.m + 2) → DirectScalarQ P.extendedDirectLd =>
   116	          (projX (directPointToPauli P u), projZ (directPointToPauli P u))) =
   117	        fun u => (Equiv.prodCongr (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)
   118	          (directBlockToPauliEquiv P)) (projX u, projZ u) := rfl
   119	  rw [hfun, ← Distribution.map_map _ (fun u => (projX u, projZ u)),
   120	    uniformDistribution_map_projX_projZ, ← uniformDistribution_prod,

     3	/-!
     4	# Products and push-forwards of finite distributions
     5	
     6	The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma presents one law both as an
     7	independent product of its generating blocks and as a dependent mixture over
     8	one of those blocks.  This module records the three rewriting rules that pass
     9	between the two presentations: a push-forward of the first factor of a product
    10	is a push-forward of the product, a product with a probability law in the
    11	second factor has the first factor as its marginal, and a push-forward of a
    12	product is the dependent mixture of the push-forwards of its second factor.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The rewriting rules support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    17	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    19	The product and mixture operations are those of blueprint
    20	`def:line-point-dist`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-! ## Nonemptiness of the support of a probability law -/
    32	
    33	/-- A law of total mass one has a nonempty support.  Blueprint
    34	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    36	theorem Distribution.support_nonempty_of_isProbability {α : Type*}
    37	    {μ : Distribution α} (hμ : μ.IsProbability) : μ.support.Nonempty := by
    38	  rw [← Finset.card_pos]
    39	  by_contra hcard
    40	  have hempty : μ.support = ∅ := by
    41	    rw [← Finset.card_eq_zero]
    42	    omega
    43	  have h1 := hμ.weight_sum_eq_one
    44	  rw [hempty] at h1
    45	  simp at h1
    46	
    47	/-! ## Push-forward of one factor of a product -/
    48	
    49	/-- Pushing the first factor of a product forward is pushing the product
    50	forward along the map acting on that factor alone.  Blueprint
    51	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    53	theorem Distribution.prod_map_left {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    54	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
    55	    (f : α → γ) :
    56	    Distribution.prod (μ.map f) ν =
    57	      (Distribution.prod μ ν).map (fun w => (f w.1, w.2)) := by
    58	  classical
    59	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    60	  · change (μ.support.image f) ×ˢ ν.support =
    61	      (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).image (fun w => (f w.1, w.2))
    62	    ext w
    63	    obtain ⟨c, y⟩ := w
    64	    simp only [Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_image, Prod.mk.injEq, Prod.exists]
    65	    constructor
    66	    · rintro ⟨⟨a, ha, rfl⟩, hy⟩
    67	      exact ⟨a, y, ⟨ha, hy⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
    68	    · rintro ⟨a, b, ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
    69	      exact ⟨⟨a, ha, rfl⟩, hb⟩
    70	  · funext w
    71	    obtain ⟨c, y⟩ := w
    72	    have hfilter :
    73	        (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => (f p.1, p.2) = (c, y)) =
    74	          (μ.support.filter (fun a => f a = c)) ×ˢ
    75	            (ν.support.filter (fun b => b = y)) := by
    76	      ext p
    77	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Prod.mk.injEq]
    78	      tauto
    79	    have hy : ∑ b ∈ ν.support.filter (fun b => b = y), ν.weight b =
    80	        ν.weight y := by
    81	      rw [Finset.filter_eq' ν.support y]
    82	      by_cases hmem : y ∈ ν.support
    83	      · rw [if_pos hmem, Finset.sum_singleton]
    84	      · rw [if_neg hmem, Finset.sum_empty, ν.outsideSupport y hmem]

    86	      ∑ p ∈ (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => (f p.1, p.2) = (c, y)),
    87	        μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2
    88	    rw [hfilter, Finset.sum_product,
    89	      Finset.sum_congr rfl
    90	        (fun a _ => (Finset.mul_sum (ν.support.filter (fun b => b = y))

    92	      hy, ← Finset.sum_mul]
    93	    rfl
    94	
    95	/-! ## The first marginal of a product -/
    96	
    97	/-- The first marginal of a product whose second factor is a probability law
    98	is the first factor.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

   102	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).map Prod.fst = μ := by
   103	  classical
   104	  obtain ⟨b₀, hb₀⟩ := Distribution.support_nonempty_of_isProbability hν
   105	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   106	  · change (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).image Prod.fst = μ.support
   107	    ext a
   108	    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_product, Prod.exists]
   109	    constructor
   110	    · rintro ⟨x, y, ⟨hx, -⟩, rfl⟩
   111	      exact hx
   112	    · intro ha
   113	      exact ⟨a, b₀, ⟨ha, hb₀⟩, rfl⟩
   114	  · funext a
   115	    have hfilter : (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => p.1 = a) =
   116	        (μ.support.filter (fun x => x = a)) ×ˢ ν.support := by
   117	      ext p
   118	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product]
   119	      tauto
   120	    have ha : ∑ x ∈ μ.support.filter (fun x => x = a), μ.weight x =
   121	        μ.weight a := by
   122	      rw [Finset.filter_eq' μ.support a]
   123	      by_cases hmem : a ∈ μ.support
   124	      · rw [if_pos hmem, Finset.sum_singleton]
   125	      · rw [if_neg hmem, Finset.sum_empty, μ.outsideSupport a hmem]
   126	    change (∑ p ∈ (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => p.1 = a),
   127	      μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) = μ.weight a
   128	    rw [hfilter, Finset.sum_product,
   129	      Finset.sum_congr rfl
   130	        (fun x _ => (Finset.mul_sum ν.support (fun b => ν.weight b)
   131	          (μ.weight x)).symm),
   132	      hν.weight_sum_eq_one]
   133	    simpa using ha
   134	
   135	/-- Reading a function of the first factor of a product whose second factor is
   136	a probability law is reading it on the first factor.  Blueprint
   137	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   138	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   139	theorem Distribution.prod_map_of_fst {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   140	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
   141	    (hν : ν.IsProbability) (h : α → γ) :
   142	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).map (fun w => h w.1) = μ.map h := by
   143	  rw [← Distribution.map_map (Distribution.prod μ ν) Prod.fst h,
   144	    Distribution.prod_map_fst μ ν hν]
   145	
   146	/-! ## A product as a dependent mixture -/
   147	
   148	/-- A push-forward of a product is the dependent mixture, over the first
   149	factor, of the push-forwards of the second factor.  Blueprint
   150	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   151	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   152	theorem Distribution.prod_map_eq_bind {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   153	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
   154	    (g : α × β → γ) :
   155	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).map g =
   156	      Distribution.bind μ (fun a => ν.map (fun b => g (a, b))) := by
   157	  classical
   158	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   159	  · change (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).image g =
   160	      μ.support.biUnion (fun a => ν.support.image (fun b => g (a, b)))
   161	    ext c
   162	    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_biUnion, Finset.mem_product,
   163	      Prod.exists]
   164	    constructor
   165	    · rintro ⟨a, b, ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl⟩
   166	      exact ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
   167	    · rintro ⟨a, ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
   168	      exact ⟨a, b, ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl⟩
   169	  · funext c
   170	    change (∑ p ∈ (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => g p = c),
   171	        μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2) =
   172	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support, μ.weight a *
   173	        ∑ b ∈ ν.support.filter (fun b => g (a, b) = c), ν.weight b
   174	    rw [Finset.sum_filter, Finset.sum_product]
   175	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => ?_
   176	    rw [Finset.sum_filter, Finset.mul_sum]
   177	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => ?_
   178	    by_cases h : g (a, b) = c
   179	    · rw [if_pos h, if_pos h]
   180	    · rw [if_neg h, if_neg h, mul_zero]
   181	
   182	end
   183	
   184	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     3	/-!
     4	# Reshuffling products of finitely supported laws
     5	
     6	The sampling procedure of the sub-line lemma produces its six independent
     7	generating blocks in one grouping, while the restricted line-point laws that
     8	the projected marginals must match present the same six blocks in another
     9	grouping.  This module records the rewriting rules that pass between two such
    10	presentations: the support and the weight of a product, the fact that a
    11	push-forward along a bijection is determined by the supports and weights it
    12	compares, and the push-forward of the second factor of a product.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The rewriting rules support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    17	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    19	The product operation is that of blueprint
    20	`def:line-point-dist`.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-! ## The support and the weight of a product -/
    32	
    33	/-- The support of a product law is the product of the supports.  Blueprint
    34	`def:line-point-dist`, paper
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    36	-/
    37	theorem Distribution.prod_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    38	    [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) :
    39	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).support = μ.support ×ˢ ν.support := rfl
    40	
    41	/-- The weight of a product law is the product of the weights.  Blueprint
    42	`def:line-point-dist`, paper
    43	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:274-287`.
    44	-/
    45	theorem Distribution.prod_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    46	    [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) (w : α × β) :
    47	    (Distribution.prod μ ν).weight w = μ.weight w.1 * ν.weight w.2 := rfl
    48	
    49	/-! ## Push-forward along a bijection -/
    50	
    51	/-- A push-forward along a bijection is identified by the supports and the
    52	weights it compares: if the map matches the two supports and carries each
    53	weight to the corresponding weight, and if it has a two-sided inverse, the
    54	push-forward is the target law.  Blueprint
    55	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    56	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    57	theorem Distribution.map_bijective_eq {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    58	    [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β) (f : α → β)
    59	    (g : β → α) (hgf : ∀ a, g (f a) = a) (hfg : ∀ b, f (g b) = b)
    60	    (hs : ∀ a, a ∈ μ.support ↔ f a ∈ ν.support)
    61	    (hw : ∀ a, μ.weight a = ν.weight (f a)) :
    62	    μ.map f = ν := by
    63	  classical
    64	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    65	  · rw [Distribution.map_support]
    66	    ext b
    67	    simp only [Finset.mem_image]
    68	    constructor
    69	    · rintro ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩
    70	      exact (hs a).mp ha
    71	    · intro hb
    72	      refine ⟨g b, (hs (g b)).mpr ?_, hfg b⟩
    73	      rw [hfg b]
    74	      exact hb
    75	  · funext b
    76	    rw [Distribution.map_weight]
    77	    have hfilter : μ.support.filter (fun a => f a = b) =
    78	        μ.support.filter (fun a => a = g b) := by
    79	      ext a
    80	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
    81	      constructor
    82	      · rintro ⟨ha, h⟩
    83	        exact ⟨ha, by rw [← h, hgf]⟩
    84	      · rintro ⟨ha, h⟩
    85	        exact ⟨ha, by rw [h, hfg]⟩
    86	    rw [hfilter, Finset.filter_eq' μ.support (g b)]
    87	    by_cases hmem : g b ∈ μ.support
    88	    · rw [if_pos hmem, Finset.sum_singleton, hw (g b), hfg]
    89	    · rw [if_neg hmem, Finset.sum_empty]
    90	      refine (ν.outsideSupport b ?_).symm
    91	      intro hb
    92	      exact hmem ((hs (g b)).mpr (by rw [hfg b]; exact hb))
    93	
    94	/-! ## Push-forward of the second factor of a product -/
    95	
    96	/-- Pushing the second factor of a product forward is pushing the product
    97	forward along the map acting on that factor alone.  Blueprint
    98	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    99	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   100	theorem Distribution.prod_map_right {α β γ : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
   101	    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
   102	    (g : β → γ) :
   103	    Distribution.prod μ (ν.map g) =
   104	      (Distribution.prod μ ν).map (fun w => (w.1, g w.2)) := by
   105	  classical
   106	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
   107	  · change μ.support ×ˢ (ν.support.image g) =
   108	      (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).image (fun w => (w.1, g w.2))
   109	    ext w
   110	    obtain ⟨x, c⟩ := w
   111	    simp only [Finset.mem_product, Finset.mem_image, Prod.mk.injEq, Prod.exists]
   112	    constructor
   113	    · rintro ⟨hx, b, hb, rfl⟩
   114	      exact ⟨x, b, ⟨hx, hb⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
   115	    · rintro ⟨a, b, ⟨ha, hb⟩, rfl, rfl⟩
   116	      exact ⟨ha, b, hb, rfl⟩
   117	  · funext w
   118	    obtain ⟨x, c⟩ := w
   119	    have hfilter :
   120	        (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => (p.1, g p.2) = (x, c)) =
   121	          (μ.support.filter (fun a => a = x)) ×ˢ
   122	            (ν.support.filter (fun b => g b = c)) := by
   123	      ext p
   124	      simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product, Prod.mk.injEq]
   125	      tauto
   126	    have hx : ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter (fun a => a = x), μ.weight a =
   127	        μ.weight x := by
   128	      rw [Finset.filter_eq' μ.support x]
   129	      by_cases hmem : x ∈ μ.support
   130	      · rw [if_pos hmem, Finset.sum_singleton]
   131	      · rw [if_neg hmem, Finset.sum_empty, μ.outsideSupport x hmem]
   132	    change μ.weight x * (ν.map g).weight c =
   133	      ∑ p ∈ (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun p => (p.1, g p.2) = (x, c)),
   134	        μ.weight p.1 * ν.weight p.2
   135	    rw [hfilter, Finset.sum_product,
   136	      Finset.sum_congr rfl (fun a _ =>
   137	        (Finset.mul_sum (ν.support.filter (fun b => g b = c))
   138	          (fun b => ν.weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm),
   139	      ← Finset.sum_mul, hx]
   140	    rfl
   141	
   142	end
   143	
   144	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

     5	
     6	This module splits the fresh diagonal direction pair of the sub-line sampling
     7	procedure into its two independent blocks.  The coordinate-index event
     8	constrains only the scalar seed of the pair, so conditioning on it leaves the
     9	direction block uniform and independent of the conditioned seed.  The
    10	direction block of a fresh pair is therefore available as an unconstrained
    11	uniform vector, which is what allows the sampling procedure to read it off the
    12	corresponding block of the direction of the sampled extended line.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The block decomposition supports `lem:qld-sublines` in
    17	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    19	The coordinate-index event is that of `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint
    20	lines 1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    21	-/

    23	open scoped BigOperators
    24	
    25	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    26	
    27	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    28	
    29	noncomputable section
    30	
    31	/-! ## Conditioning the first factor of a product -/
    32	
    33	/-- Restricting a product law to an event depending on the first factor alone
    34	leaves the second factor unchanged and independent of the conditioned first
    35	factor.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    36	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    37	theorem Distribution.restrict_prod_fst {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α]
    38	    [DecidableEq β] (μ : Distribution α) (ν : Distribution β)
    39	    (hν : ν.IsProbability) (p : α → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    40	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a)
    41	    (hpos' : 0 < ∑ w ∈ (Distribution.prod μ ν).support.filter
    42	        (fun w => p w.1), (Distribution.prod μ ν).weight w) :
    43	    Distribution.restrict (Distribution.prod μ ν) (fun w => p w.1) hpos' =
    44	      Distribution.prod (Distribution.restrict μ p hpos) ν := by
    45	  classical
    46	  have hsupp : (Distribution.prod μ ν).support.filter (fun w => p w.1) =
    47	      (μ.support.filter p) ×ˢ ν.support := by
    48	    change (μ.support ×ˢ ν.support).filter (fun w => p w.1) =
    49	      (μ.support.filter p) ×ˢ ν.support
    50	    ext w
    51	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_product]
    52	    tauto
    53	  have hmass : (∑ w ∈ (Distribution.prod μ ν).support.filter
    54	        (fun w => p w.1), (Distribution.prod μ ν).weight w) =
    55	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, μ.weight a := by
    56	    rw [hsupp]

    58	        (Distribution.prod μ ν).weight w) =
    59	        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter p, ∑ b ∈ ν.support,
    60	          μ.weight a * ν.weight b := by
    61	      rw [Finset.sum_product]
    62	      rfl
    63	    rw [h1, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ =>
    64	        (Finset.mul_sum ν.support (fun b => ν.weight b) (μ.weight a)).symm,
    65	      hν.weight_sum_eq_one]
    66	    simp
    67	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    68	  · change (Distribution.prod μ ν).support.filter (fun w => p w.1) =
    69	      (μ.support.filter p) ×ˢ ν.support
    70	    exact hsupp
    71	  · funext w
    72	    change (if p w.1 then (Distribution.prod μ ν).weight w /
    73	        ∑ c ∈ (Distribution.prod μ ν).support.filter (fun w => p w.1),

     3	/-!
     4	# Generating laws of the restricted line-point distributions
     5	
     6	This module rewrites the two restricted line-point laws of
     7	`def:ith-restricted-line` as push-forwards of a single uniformly sampled
     8	low-degree vector conditioned on the coordinate-index fiber of its retained
     9	scalar seed.  In that form the point block, the seed and the direction block
    10	of the sampled vector are visibly the independent generating data of the
    11	restricted law, which is the description used by the sampling procedure of the
    12	sub-line lemma: there the projected pairs are built either from a direction
    13	block inherited from the extended line or from freshly sampled data, and each
    14	is asserted to follow a restricted law.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	The generating descriptions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    19	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    21	The restricted laws themselves are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    22	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    23	-/

    33	/-! ## Restriction of a push-forward -/
    34	
    35	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: restricting a push-forward distribution to a
    36	decidable event is the push-forward of the restriction to the pre-image of
    37	that event.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    39	theorem Distribution.restrict_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    40	    (μ : Distribution α) (f : α → β) (p : β → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    41	    (q : α → Prop) [DecidablePred q] (hq : ∀ a, q a ↔ p (f a))
    42	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ b ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight b)
    43	    (hpos' : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight a) :
    44	    Distribution.restrict (μ.map f) p hpos =
    45	      (Distribution.restrict μ q hpos').map f := by
    46	  classical
    47	  have hfiber : ∀ b : β, p b →
    48	      μ.support.filter (fun a => f a = b) =
    49	        (μ.support.filter q).filter (fun a => f a = b) := by
    50	    intro b hb
    51	    ext a
    52	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
    53	    constructor
    54	    · rintro ⟨ha, hab⟩
    55	      exact ⟨⟨ha, (hq a).mpr (hab ▸ hb)⟩, hab⟩
    56	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha, -⟩, hab⟩
    57	      exact ⟨ha, hab⟩
    58	  have himg : (μ.map f).support.filter p = (μ.support.filter q).image f := by
    59	    ext b
    60	    simp only [Distribution.map_support, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_image]
    61	    constructor
    62	    · rintro ⟨⟨a, ha, rfl⟩, hpb⟩
    63	      exact ⟨a, ⟨ha, (hq a).mpr hpb⟩, rfl⟩
    64	    · rintro ⟨a, ⟨ha1, ha2⟩, rfl⟩
    65	      exact ⟨⟨a, ha1, rfl⟩, (hq a).mp ha2⟩
    66	  have hmass : (∑ b ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight b) =
    67	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight a := by
    68	    rw [himg]
    69	    rw [← Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    70	      (s := μ.support.filter q) (t := (μ.support.filter q).image f)
    71	      (g := f) (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image_of_mem f ha) μ.weight]
    72	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
    73	    obtain ⟨a0, ha0, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hb
    74	    rw [Distribution.map_weight,
    75	      hfiber _ ((hq a0).mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha0).2)]
    76	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    77	  · exact himg
    78	  · funext b
    79	    show (if p b then (μ.map f).weight b /
    80	        ∑ c ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight c else 0) =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ (μ.support.filter q).filter (fun a => f a = b),
    82	        (if q a then μ.weight a / ∑ c ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight c else 0)
    83	    by_cases hb : p b
    84	    · rw [if_pos hb, hmass, Distribution.map_weight, hfiber b hb,
    85	        Finset.sum_div]
    86	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
    87	      rw [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1).2]
    88	    · rw [if_neg hb]
    89	      refine (Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha => ?_).symm
    90	      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
    91	      exact absurd (ha2 ▸ (hq a).mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha1).2) hb

     5	/-!
     6	# Distribution infrastructure for the low individual degree test
     7	
     8	Shared distribution definitions: finite-support weighted distributions,
     9	a probability predicate, push-forward distributions, weighted-sum linear maps,
    10	averaging, uniform distribution, and outcome summation.
    11	
    12	Note: this module contributes declarations to the comparator statement closure
    13	of `mainFormal`, which must elaborate in the same environment as the
    14	Mathlib-only `Challenge.lean`.  Keep the full `import Mathlib`; do not narrow
    15	it.  See `docs/comparator.md`, "Environment alignment".
    16	-/
    17	
    18	open scoped BigOperators MatrixOrder Matrix ComplexOrder
    19	
    20	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT
    21	
    22	/-- A finite-support weighted distribution with nonnegative real-valued weights. -/
    23	structure Distribution (α : Type*) where
    24	  support : Finset α := ∅
    25	  weight : α → Error := fun _ => 0
    26	  nonnegative : ∀ a, 0 ≤ weight a := by intro _; positivity
    27	  outsideSupport : ∀ a, a ∉ support → weight a = 0 := by intro _ _; rfl
    28	
    29	namespace Distribution
    30	
    31	/-- The total mass carried by the explicit support of a distribution. -/
    32	def totalWeight {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Error :=
    33	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a
    34	
    35	/-- A `Distribution` is probabilistic when its total mass is exactly `1`. -/
    36	def IsProbability {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : Prop :=
    37	  𝒟.totalWeight = 1
    38	
    39	/-- Push a finite-support distribution forward along a map.
    40	
    41	This is the project `Distribution` analogue of `PMF.map`.  The support is the
    42	image of the original finite support, and each new weight is the sum of the
    43	weights in the corresponding fiber. -/
    44	noncomputable def map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    45	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) : Distribution β where
    46	  support := 𝒟.support.image e
    47	  weight := fun b => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a
    48	  nonnegative := fun _ => Finset.sum_nonneg fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a
    49	  outsideSupport := fun _ hb =>
    50	    Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha =>
    51	      (hb (Finset.mem_image.mpr
    52	        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim
    53	
    54	@[simp]
    55	theorem map_support {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    56	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    57	    (𝒟.map e).support = 𝒟.support.image e := rfl
    58	
    59	@[simp]
    60	theorem map_weight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    61	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (b : β) :
    62	    (𝒟.map e).weight b =
    63	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a := rfl
    64	
    65	/-- Push-forward preserves total mass. -/
    66	theorem map_totalWeight {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    67	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) :
    68	    (𝒟.map e).totalWeight = 𝒟.totalWeight := by
    69	  simpa [totalWeight, map] using
    70	    (Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    71	      (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    72	      (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩) 𝒟.weight)
    73	
    74	/-- A finite weighted sum over a push-forward distribution is the corresponding
    75	weighted sum of the pulled-back family.  This is the `Distribution` analogue of
    76	the finite-sum form of `PMF.map`. -/
    77	theorem map_sum_smul {α β M : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    78	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    79	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → M) :
    80	    ∑ b ∈ (𝒟.map e).support, (𝒟.map e).weight b • f b =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    82	  classical
    83	  calc
    84	    ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    85	        (∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a) • f b
    86	        = ∑ b ∈ 𝒟.support.image e,
    87	            ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b), 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    88	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    89	          intro b _
    90	          rw [Finset.sum_smul]
    91	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    92	          intro a ha
    93	          exact congrArg (fun x => 𝒟.weight a • f x) (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2.symm
    94	    _ = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f (e a) := by
    95	          exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    96	            (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)
    97	            (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨a, ha, rfl⟩)
    98	            (fun a => 𝒟.weight a • f (e a))
    99	
   100	end Distribution

   102	/-- On a finite ambient type, a summand that vanishes outside a distribution's
   103	explicit support has the same total sum over all ambient values as over that support.
   104	
   105	This is a project-local explicit-support adapter around Mathlib's `Finset.sum_subset`:
   106	Mathlib supplies the finite-sum theorem, while this lemma packages the common shape used
   107	when paper expressions sum over a whole question set but the repository stores a smaller
   108	`Distribution.support`.  It is not intended to replace Mathlib probability theory. -/
   109	theorem Distribution.sum_univ_eq_sum_support {α β : Type*} [Fintype α]
   110	    [AddCommMonoid β] (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → β)
   111	    (hf : ∀ a, a ∉ 𝒟.support → f a = 0) :
   112	    (∑ a : α, f a) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, f a := by
   113	  classical
   114	  simpa using
   115	    (Finset.sum_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
   116	      (fun a _ ha => hf a ha)).symm
   117	
   118	namespace Distribution.IsProbability
   119	
   120	/-- Unpack the equality form of the probability invariant. -/
   121	theorem weight_sum_eq_one {α : Type*}
   122	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   123	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
   124	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.totalWeight] using h𝒟
   125	
   126	/-- A probability distribution has total weight one over any finite superset
   127	of its explicit support. -/
   128	theorem weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset {α : Type*}
   129	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) {s : Finset α}
   130	    (hsubset : 𝒟.support ⊆ s) :
   131	    ∑ a ∈ s, 𝒟.weight a = 1 := by
   132	  have hsum :
   133	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a = ∑ a ∈ s, 𝒟.weight a :=
   134	    Finset.sum_subset hsubset (fun a _ ha => 𝒟.outsideSupport a ha)
   135	  exact hsum ▸ h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   136	
   137	/-- On a finite ambient type, a probabilistic `Distribution` has total weight `1` even
   138	when its weights are summed over the whole ambient type.
   139	
   140	This packages the explicit-support bookkeeping in `Distribution` for downstream Lean
   141	statements that follow the paper's notation `𝔼_{x ∼ 𝒟}` over the question set rather
   142	than over a stored support finset. -/
   143	theorem weight_sum_univ_eq_one {α : Type*} [Fintype α]
   144	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   145	    (∑ a : α, 𝒟.weight a) = 1 := by
   146	  simpa using h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one_of_subset (Finset.subset_univ 𝒟.support)
   147	
   148	/-- A probability distribution has total weight at most `1`. -/
   149	theorem weight_sum_le_one {α : Type*}
   150	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) :
   151	    ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a ≤ 1 :=
   152	  le_of_eq h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one
   153	
   154	/-- Push-forward preserves the probability invariant. -/
   155	theorem map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   156	    {𝒟 : Distribution α} (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   157	    (𝒟.map e).IsProbability := by
   158	  simpa [Distribution.IsProbability, Distribution.map_totalWeight] using h𝒟
   159	
   160	end Distribution.IsProbability

   162	namespace Distribution
   163	
   164	/-- The Mathlib probability mass function associated to a project `Distribution`
   165	whose total mass is one.
   166	
   167	The construction sends each nonnegative real weight to `ℝ≥0∞` by
   168	`ENNReal.ofReal`; the hypotheses of `PMF.ofFinset` are exactly the project
   169	probability invariant and the stored zero-off-support condition. -/
   170	noncomputable def toPMF {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   171	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) : PMF α :=
   172	  PMF.ofFinset (fun a => ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a)) 𝒟.support
   173	    (by
   174	      rw [← ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a),
   175	        h𝒟.weight_sum_eq_one]
   176	      simp)
   177	    (by
   178	      intro a ha
   179	      rw [𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   180	      simp)

   182	@[simp]
   183	theorem toPMF_apply {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   184	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :
   185	    𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a = ENNReal.ofReal (𝒟.weight a) := rfl
   186	
   187	@[simp]
   188	theorem toPMF_apply_toReal {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   189	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (a : α) :
   190	    (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a).toReal = 𝒟.weight a := by
   191	  rw [toPMF_apply, ENNReal.toReal_ofReal (𝒟.nonnegative a)]
   192	
   193	/-- The associated PMF has zero mass outside the stored support of the project
   194	distribution. -/
   195	theorem toPMF_apply_of_notMem {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α)
   196	    (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) {a : α} (ha : a ∉ 𝒟.support) :
   197	    𝒟.toPMF h𝒟 a = 0 := by
   198	  rw [toPMF_apply, 𝒟.outsideSupport a ha]
   199	  simp
   200	
   201	/-- The project push-forward agrees with Mathlib's push-forward of the
   202	associated probability mass function. -/
   203	theorem toPMF_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
   204	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (h𝒟 : 𝒟.IsProbability) (e : α → β) :
   205	    (𝒟.map e).toPMF (h𝒟.map e) = (𝒟.toPMF h𝒟).map e := by
   206	  classical
   207	  ext b
   208	  rw [toPMF_apply, PMF.map_apply, map_weight]
   209	  rw [ENNReal.ofReal_sum_of_nonneg
   210	    (s := 𝒟.support.filter (fun a => e a = b))
   211	    (fun a _ => 𝒟.nonnegative a)]
   212	  rw [tsum_eq_sum (s := 𝒟.support)]
   213	  · rw [Finset.sum_filter]
   214	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   215	    intro a ha
   216	    by_cases hea : e a = b
   217	    · have hba : b = e a := hea.symm
   218	      rw [if_pos hea, if_pos hba, toPMF_apply]
   219	    · have hba : b ≠ e a := fun hba => hea hba.symm
   220	      rw [if_neg hea, if_neg hba]
   221	  · intro a ha
   222	    by_cases hba : b = e a
   223	    · rw [if_pos hba, toPMF_apply_of_notMem 𝒟 h𝒟 ha]
   224	    · rw [if_neg hba]
   225	
   226	end Distribution
   227	
   228	/-- Average a scalar function against the stored finite support of a distribution. -/
   229	def avgOver {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → Error) : Error :=
   230	  ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a * f a
   231	
   232	namespace Distribution
   233	
   234	/-- The module-valued weighted finite sum associated to a finite-support `Distribution`,
   235	as a linear map in the averaged family.
   236	
   237	This packages the finite-support expression underlying both scalar averages and
   238	operator averages.  It keeps the explicit support carried by `Distribution`,
   239	while exposing the `Error`-module structure of the weighted sum. -/
   240	noncomputable def weightedSumLinearMap (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
   241	    {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) : (α → M) →ₗ[Error] M where
   242	  toFun := fun f => ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a
   243	  map_add' := fun f g => by
   244	    simp only [Pi.add_apply, smul_add, Finset.sum_add_distrib]
   245	  map_smul' := fun c f => by
   246	    simp only [Pi.smul_apply]
   247	    calc
   248	      ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • c • f a =
   249	          ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, c • (𝒟.weight a • f a) := by
   250	            refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
   251	            intro a _
   252	            rw [smul_smul, smul_smul, mul_comm]
   253	      _ = c • ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a := by
   254	            rw [Finset.smul_sum]
   255	
   256	@[simp]
   257	theorem weightedSumLinearMap_apply (M : Type*) [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
   258	    {α : Type*} (𝒟 : Distribution α) (f : α → M) :
   259	    𝒟.weightedSumLinearMap M f = ∑ a ∈ 𝒟.support, 𝒟.weight a • f a :=
   260	  rfl

   455	  · exact Distribution.IsProbability.map (subLineRawDist_isProbability P) _
   456	  · exact Distribution.IsProbability.map (subLineRawDist_isProbability P) _
   457	
   458	/-- The index-first decomposition of an extended direct sample, read at the
   459	bare extended dimension.  This is the decomposition
   460	`directLdSpaceIndexEquiv` of `def:ld-question-distribution` with its stored
   461	coordinate typed by the bare dimension `2 m + 2`. -/
   462	private def subLineSampleEquiv (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   463	    DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd ≃
   464	      Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLinePointDir P where
   465	  toFun s := (s.index, s.point, s.direction)
   466	  invFun w := ⟨w.2.1, w.1, w.2.2⟩
   467	  left_inv s := by cases s; rfl
   468	  right_inv w := by cases w; rfl
   469	
   470	/-- The extended-line marginal of one branch of the sub-line law is the law of
   471	the canonical line of the corresponding kind through a uniformly sampled
   472	extended direct sample.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   473	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   474	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_fst (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind) :
   475	    (subLineBranchDist P kind).map Prod.fst =
   476	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   477	        (subLineExtLineOfSample P kind) := by
   478	  classical
   479	  have hstep1 : (subLineBranchDist P kind).map Prod.fst =
   480	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
   481	        (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   482	            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   483	              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
   484	          fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.1.1, k, w.1.2⟩ := by
   485	    rw [subLineBranchDist, Distribution.map_map, subLineRawDist,
   486	      Distribution.bind_map]
   487	    refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
   488	    rw [Distribution.map_map]
   489	    rfl
   490	  have hstep2 : ∀ k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2),
   491	      (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   492	          (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   493	            (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
   494	        (fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.1.1, k, w.1.2⟩) =
   495	      (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P)).map
   496	        (fun pd => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨pd.1, k, pd.2⟩) := by
   497	    intro k
   498	    exact Distribution.prod_map_of_fst
   499	      (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   500	      (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   501	        (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))
   502	      (Distribution.prod_isProbability
   503	        (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
   504	        (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k))
   505	        (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P (subLineXIndex P k))
   506	        (subLineSeedDist_isProbability P (subLineZIndex P k)))
   507	      (fun pd => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨pd.1, k, pd.2⟩)
   508	  have hstep3 :
   509	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) (fun k =>
   510	        (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P)).map
   511	          (fun pd => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨pd.1, k, pd.2⟩)) =
   512	      (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLinePointDir P)).map
   513	        (fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.2.1, w.1, w.2.2⟩) := by
   514	    rw [uniformDistribution_prod (Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) (SubLinePointDir P)]
   515	    exact (Distribution.prod_map_eq_bind
   516	      (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2)))
   517	      (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
   518	      (fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.2.1, w.1, w.2.2⟩)).symm
   519	  have hstep4 :
   520	      (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2) × SubLinePointDir P)).map
   521	        (fun w => subLineExtLineOfSample P kind ⟨w.2.1, w.1, w.2.2⟩) =
   522	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace P.extendedDirectLd)).map
   523	        (subLineExtLineOfSample P kind) := by
   524	    rw [← uniformDistribution_map_equiv (subLineSampleEquiv P),
   525	      Distribution.map_map]
   526	    rfl
   527	  rw [hstep1, Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ (fun k _ => hstep2 k),
   528	    hstep3, hstep4]

   530	/-- The extended-line marginal of the sub-line law is the extended-line
   531	marginal of the directly indexed line-point law.  Blueprint
   532	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   533	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   534	theorem subLineDist_map_fst (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   535	    (subLineDist P).map Prod.fst =
   536	      (directLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst := by
   537	  classical
   538	  have haxis : (subLineBranchDist P .axis).map Prod.fst =
   539	      (directALinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst := by
   540	    rw [subLineBranchDist_map_fst, directALinePointDist, Distribution.map_map]
   541	    rfl
   542	  have hdiag : (subLineBranchDist P .diagonal).map Prod.fst =
   543	      (directDLinePointDist P.extendedDirectLd).map Prod.fst := by
   544	    rw [subLineBranchDist_map_fst, directDLinePointDist, Distribution.map_map]
   545	    rfl
   546	  rw [subLineDist, Distribution.bind_map, directLinePointDist,
   547	    ← Distribution.bind_uniform_fin_two, Distribution.bind_map]
   548	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun c _ => ?_
   549	  fin_cases c
   550	  · exact haxis
   551	  · exact hdiag

     3	/-!
     4	# The projected mixtures of the sub-line law
     5	
     6	This module assembles the two projected point marginals of the sub-line law of
     7	`lem:qld-sublines` into mixtures of the restricted product laws.  Drawing a
     8	uniform point of the extended line of a mixture of line laws is the same
     9	mixture of the corresponding uniform-point laws, so the two projected
    10	marginals of the sub-line law are the mixtures, over the drawn kind and the
    11	drawn extended coordinate, of the projected marginals of one branch at one
    12	extended coordinate.  Each of those is the component law of the pair of
    13	indices carried by that branch, so the mixing law is the law of the kind
    14	together with the pair of indices assigned to a uniform extended coordinate.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	The assembly is the last step of the proof of `lem:qld-sublines` in
    19	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    21	The restricted laws are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    22	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-! ## The uniform point of a mixture of line laws -/
    34	
    35	/-- Drawing a uniform point of the extended line of a mixture of line-triple
    36	laws is the corresponding mixture of the uniform-point laws.  Blueprint
    37	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    39	theorem subLinePointDist_bind (P : AdmissibleParams) {α : Type*}
    40	    (μ : Distribution α) (ν : α → Distribution (SubLineTriple P)) :
    41	    subLinePointDist P (Distribution.bind μ ν) =
    42	      Distribution.bind μ (fun a => subLinePointDist P (ν a)) := by
    43	  classical
    44	  unfold subLinePointDist
    45	  rw [Distribution.prod_bind_left, Distribution.bind_map]
    46	
    47	/-! ## The projected marginals of one branch at one extended coordinate -/
    48	
    49	/-- One branch of the sampling procedure, read at a fixed extended coordinate,
    50	is the law of the triple decoded from the auxiliary randomness of that
    51	coordinate.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    52	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    53	theorem subLineBranchDist_eq_bind (P : AdmissibleParams) (kind : LineKind) :
    54	    subLineBranchDist P kind =
    55	      Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))) fun k =>
    56	        (Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    57	            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    58	              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
    59	          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w := by
    60	  classical
    61	  rw [subLineBranchDist, subLineRawDist, Distribution.bind_map]
    62	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
    63	  rw [Distribution.map_map]
    64	
    65	/-- The `X` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch at
    66	one extended coordinate is the `X` component law of the pair of indices of
    67	that branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    68	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    69	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection_at (P : AdmissibleParams)
    70	    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) :
    71	    (subLinePointDist P
    72	        ((Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    73	            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    74	              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
    75	          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w)).map subLineXProjection =
    76	      subLineXComponentDist P
    77	        (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k)) := by
    78	  classical
    79	  unfold subLinePointDist
    80	  rw [Distribution.prod_map_left, Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
    81	  exact subLineBranchRaw_map_projX P kind k
    82	
    83	/-- The `Z` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch at
    84	one extended coordinate is the `Z` component law of the pair of indices of
    85	that branch.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    86	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    87	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection_at (P : AdmissibleParams)
    88	    (kind : LineKind) (k : Fin (2 * P.m + 2)) :
    89	    (subLinePointDist P
    90	        ((Distribution.prod (uniformDistribution (SubLinePointDir P))
    91	            (Distribution.prod (subLineSeedDist P (subLineXIndex P k))
    92	              (subLineSeedDist P (subLineZIndex P k)))).map
    93	          fun w => subLineTripleOf P kind k w)).map subLineZProjection =
    94	      subLineZComponentDist P
    95	        (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k)) := by
    96	  classical
    97	  unfold subLinePointDist
    98	  rw [Distribution.prod_map_left, Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
    99	  exact subLineBranchRaw_map_projZ P kind k

   101	/-! ## The mixing law of the two indices -/
   102	
   103	/-- The law of the kind and the pair of source indices assigned to a uniform
   104	extended coordinate of one branch.  Blueprint
   105	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   106	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   107	noncomputable def subLineComponentBranch (P : AdmissibleParams)
   108	    (kind : LineKind) : Distribution (SubLineComponent P) :=
   109	  (uniformDistribution (Fin (2 * P.m + 2))).map fun k =>
   110	    (kind, (subLineXIndex P k, subLineZIndex P k))
   111	
   112	/-- The mixing law of the sub-line lemma: the equal mixture over the two kinds
   113	of the law of the pair of source indices of a uniform extended coordinate.
   114	Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   115	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   116	noncomputable def subLineComponentDist (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   117	    Distribution (SubLineComponent P) :=
   118	  Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution (Fin 2))
   119	    ![subLineComponentBranch P .axis, subLineComponentBranch P .diagonal]
   120	
   121	/-- The mixing law has total mass one. -/
   122	theorem subLineComponentDist_isProbability (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   123	    (subLineComponentDist P).IsProbability := by
   124	  refine Distribution.bind_isProbability _ _
   125	    (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) fun c _ => ?_
   126	  fin_cases c
   127	  · exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   128	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) _
   129	  · exact Distribution.IsProbability.map
   130	      (uniformDistribution_isProbability _) _
   131	
   132	/-! ## The two projected marginals of one branch -/
   133	
   134	/-- The `X` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch is
   135	the mixture, along the pair of source indices of a uniform extended
   136	coordinate, of the `X` component laws.  Blueprint
   137	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   138	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   139	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection (P : AdmissibleParams)
   140	    (kind : LineKind) :
   141	    (subLinePointDist P (subLineBranchDist P kind)).map subLineXProjection =
   142	      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentBranch P kind)
   143	        (subLineXComponentDist P) := by
   144	  classical
   145	  rw [subLineBranchDist_eq_bind, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
   146	    subLineComponentBranch, Distribution.bind_map_left]
   147	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
   148	  exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection_at P kind k
   149	
   150	/-- The `Z` marginal of a uniform point of the extended line of one branch is
   151	the mixture, along the pair of source indices of a uniform extended
   152	coordinate, of the `Z` component laws.  Blueprint
   153	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   154	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   155	theorem subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection (P : AdmissibleParams)
   156	    (kind : LineKind) :
   157	    (subLinePointDist P (subLineBranchDist P kind)).map subLineZProjection =
   158	      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentBranch P kind)
   159	        (subLineZComponentDist P) := by
   160	  classical
   161	  rw [subLineBranchDist_eq_bind, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
   162	    subLineComponentBranch, Distribution.bind_map_left]
   163	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun k _ => ?_
   164	  exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection_at P kind k
   165	
   166	/-! ## The two projected marginals of the sub-line law -/
   167	
   168	/-- The `X` point marginal of the sub-line law is the mixture of the `X`
   169	component laws along the mixing law.  Blueprint
   170	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   171	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   172	theorem subLineDist_map_subLineXProjection (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   173	    (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineXProjection =
   174	      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentDist P) (subLineXComponentDist P) := by
   175	  classical
   176	  rw [subLineDist, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
   177	    subLineComponentDist, Distribution.bind_bind]
   178	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun c _ => ?_
   179	  fin_cases c
   180	  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection P .axis
   181	  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineXProjection P .diagonal
   182	
   183	/-- The `Z` point marginal of the sub-line law is the mixture of the `Z`
   184	component laws along the mixing law.  Blueprint
   185	`lem:qld-sublines`, paper
   186	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
   187	theorem subLineDist_map_subLineZProjection (P : AdmissibleParams) :
   188	    (subLinePointDist P (subLineDist P)).map subLineZProjection =
   189	      Distribution.bind (subLineComponentDist P) (subLineZComponentDist P) := by
   190	  classical
   191	  rw [subLineDist, subLinePointDist_bind, Distribution.bind_map,
   192	    subLineComponentDist, Distribution.bind_bind]
   193	  refine Distribution.bind_congr_support _ _ _ fun c _ => ?_
   194	  fin_cases c
   195	  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection P .axis
   196	  · exact subLineBranchDist_map_subLineZProjection P .diagonal
   197	
   198	/-- The two one-point projected marginals of the sub-line law are mixtures of

   201	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/

     3	/-!
     4	# Generating laws of the restricted line-point distributions
     5	
     6	This module rewrites the two restricted line-point laws of
     7	`def:ith-restricted-line` as push-forwards of a single uniformly sampled
     8	low-degree vector conditioned on the coordinate-index fiber of its retained
     9	scalar seed.  In that form the point block, the seed and the direction block
    10	of the sampled vector are visibly the independent generating data of the
    11	restricted law, which is the description used by the sampling procedure of the
    12	sub-line lemma: there the projected pairs are built either from a direction
    13	block inherited from the extended line or from freshly sampled data, and each
    14	is asserted to follow a restricted law.
    15	
    16	## References
    17	
    18	The generating descriptions support `lem:qld-sublines` in
    19	blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, whose source is
    20	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`.
    21	The restricted laws themselves are `def:ith-restricted-line`, blueprint lines
    22	1209--1228, paper lines 1038--1048.
    23	-/
    24	
    25	open scoped BigOperators
    26	
    27	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    28	
    29	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    30	
    31	noncomputable section
    32	
    33	/-! ## Restriction of a push-forward -/
    34	
    35	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: restricting a push-forward distribution to a
    36	decidable event is the push-forward of the restriction to the pre-image of
    37	that event.  Blueprint `lem:qld-sublines`, paper
    38	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1063-1116`. -/
    39	theorem Distribution.restrict_map {α β : Type*} [DecidableEq α] [DecidableEq β]
    40	    (μ : Distribution α) (f : α → β) (p : β → Prop) [DecidablePred p]
    41	    (q : α → Prop) [DecidablePred q] (hq : ∀ a, q a ↔ p (f a))
    42	    (hpos : 0 < ∑ b ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight b)
    43	    (hpos' : 0 < ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight a) :
    44	    Distribution.restrict (μ.map f) p hpos =
    45	      (Distribution.restrict μ q hpos').map f := by
    46	  classical
    47	  have hfiber : ∀ b : β, p b →
    48	      μ.support.filter (fun a => f a = b) =
    49	        (μ.support.filter q).filter (fun a => f a = b) := by
    50	    intro b hb
    51	    ext a
    52	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
    53	    constructor
    54	    · rintro ⟨ha, hab⟩
    55	      exact ⟨⟨ha, (hq a).mpr (hab ▸ hb)⟩, hab⟩
    56	    · rintro ⟨⟨ha, -⟩, hab⟩
    57	      exact ⟨ha, hab⟩
    58	  have himg : (μ.map f).support.filter p = (μ.support.filter q).image f := by
    59	    ext b
    60	    simp only [Distribution.map_support, Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_image]
    61	    constructor
    62	    · rintro ⟨⟨a, ha, rfl⟩, hpb⟩
    63	      exact ⟨a, ⟨ha, (hq a).mpr hpb⟩, rfl⟩
    64	    · rintro ⟨a, ⟨ha1, ha2⟩, rfl⟩
    65	      exact ⟨⟨a, ha1, rfl⟩, (hq a).mp ha2⟩
    66	  have hmass : (∑ b ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight b) =
    67	      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight a := by
    68	    rw [himg]
    69	    rw [← Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
    70	      (s := μ.support.filter q) (t := (μ.support.filter q).image f)
    71	      (g := f) (fun a ha => Finset.mem_image_of_mem f ha) μ.weight]
    72	    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
    73	    obtain ⟨a0, ha0, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hb
    74	    rw [Distribution.map_weight,
    75	      hfiber _ ((hq a0).mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha0).2)]
    76	  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
    77	  · exact himg
    78	  · funext b
    79	    show (if p b then (μ.map f).weight b /
    80	        ∑ c ∈ (μ.map f).support.filter p, (μ.map f).weight c else 0) =
    81	      ∑ a ∈ (μ.support.filter q).filter (fun a => f a = b),
    82	        (if q a then μ.weight a / ∑ c ∈ μ.support.filter q, μ.weight c else 0)
    83	    by_cases hb : p b
    84	    · rw [if_pos hb, hmass, Distribution.map_weight, hfiber b hb,
    85	        Finset.sum_div]
    86	      refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a ha => ?_
    87	      rw [if_pos (Finset.mem_filter.mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1).2]
    88	    · rw [if_neg hb]
    89	      refine (Finset.sum_eq_zero fun a ha => ?_).symm
    90	      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
    91	      exact absurd (ha2 ▸ (hq a).mp (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha1).2) hb
    92	
    93	/-! ## The coordinate-index event on a single uniform vector -/
    94	
    95	/-- The coordinate-index event of `def:ith-restricted-line` read on the single

## Review
The prior findings are resolved: `reindexOp_nonneg` now delegates to the existing quantum API, and the `SubLinePrefix` description now matches the implemented prefix truncation.

The restricted-mixture statements match `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:1049-1061`, including the `2m` and `4m²` factors. The sub-line construction is correctly documented as a direct-carrier auxiliary rather than the unresolved source theorem.

The only `sorry` occurrences are the two pre-existing combined-lines obligations at `Lines.lean:63` and `Lines.lean:92`; both are clearly tracked as issue #18 work. No new proof-integrity bypasses were found. Exact-head local CI passed, and the diff and formatting checks are clean.

Residual risk remains the documented transport from `SubLineWitness` to the paper’s seed-indexed extended carrier; this PR does not claim that obligation is complete.
